evidence: The density and roughness of the obtained films were determined on the basis of the X-ray reflectivity data. The films deposited at 200°C had an average density of 2.1 g/cm3, which constitutes 64% of the bulk density of aluminum nitride (3.26 g/cm3). The roughness of films obtained at 200°C was from 6 to 9 Å, depending on the film thickness. However, the roughness determined by the atomic force microscope indicated showed considerably lower values. The aluminum nitride film deposited at 200°C to a thickness of ~300 Å had a roughness of ~1.5 Å (see supplemental information). According to the X-ray diffraction data, nitride films deposited in this work at 200°C had an amorphous structure. Figure 4 shows the results of X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis of an aluminum nitride film with a thickness of 1010 Å, which was deposited at 200°C with the exposure and purge parameters 1.5/60/1/70. The XPS analysis of a 475-Å AlN film revealed ~5 at % of oxygen in the bulk of the film. The hydrogen content of 1010-Å films deposited at 200°C was determined by forward recoil spectrometry before and after annealing (see supplemental information). The roughness root mean square (RMS) of aluminum nitride films was determined with an AutoProbe CP probe microscope coupled with an atomic force microscope (USA) in the contactless mode from a 2×2-μm2 surface area.
